aboutParagraphs: Little Mulberry is the wooded, technical test that Atlanta-area players graduate to after Oregon Park — 18 holes of corridor golf at par 60, built for the advanced and intermediate player. The primary layout runs 5,035 feet with a longer alternate pushing past 6,000.

It's free to play on concrete tees with DISCatcher baskets, and the park is a proper Gwinnett County destination with restrooms and good access. The woods are the course: tight lines, tree-guarded greens, and one big 850-foot par 5 to stretch your arm.
Bring your accuracy game — distance alone won't get you around Little Mulberry.

signatureHoleDescription: Hole 10 is Little Mulberry's centerpiece: 850 feet of par 5 that demands three committed shots through the corridor. From the tee you're threading a gap; from the second landing zone you're choosing a line at a green that the woods protect from every side. It's the hole that rewards patience and punishes ego.
localTips: Accuracy beats power on every hole but the signature par 5. The primary layout is the standard loop; the alternate tees add distance for advanced play. Free to play, concrete tees, and the woods will keep your disc if you don't keep your line.
